note: The knowledge graph behind the campaign (design 4.1). A topic id is also the skill tag that missions award evidence for. Loaded by game-shell/src/curriculum.cpp; validated by tests/test_content.cpp. Levels 6-50 add topics as their missions ship.

areas.title: Foundations
areas.summary: Running code and moving data in and out of it.

areas.title: Iteration
areas.summary: Doing work repeatedly without repeating yourself.

areas.title: Functions & Scope
areas.summary: Packaging behaviour so it can be reused and tested.

areas.title: Data Structures
areas.summary: Choosing the container that makes the problem easy.

areas.title: Testing & Evidence
areas.summary: Proving code works, including where you did not look.

areas.title: Debugging
areas.summary: Finding out why it does not work.

areas.title: Tooling & Version Control
areas.summary: The professional's workbench: shell and history.

areas.title: Software Engineering
areas.summary: Building things that other people can live with.

areas.title: Systems & Performance
areas.summary: How machines behave under load and at scale.

areas.title: Defensive Security
areas.summary: Keeping software and its users safe: validate input, guard secrets, fail closed.

topics.title: Running a program and printing
topics.summary: Run a file, read its output, and produce an exact line of text.
objectives: Run a program and read its output
Print a string exactly as specified

misconceptions.text: The program runs from the editor without being saved or executed.
misconceptions.remedy: Nothing runs until it is executed: write the line, then run it and watch the output pane.

topics.title: Reading standard input
topics.summary: Read the whole input, split it into tokens, and cope with an empty input.
objectives: Read all of standard input at once
Split input into tokens without assuming how many there are

misconceptions.text: There will always be at least one value on the input.
misconceptions.remedy: Guard the empty case: the tests deliberately feed a blank line. Handle it before you loop.

topics.title: Values and types
topics.summary: Know what kind of value you hold and what operations it supports.
objectives: Store a value in a named variable
Distinguish text from numbers and convert between them

misconceptions.text: Input arrives as a number ready for arithmetic.
misconceptions.remedy: Input is text until converted: parse each token with the numeric conversion before maths.

topics.title: Arithmetic and percentages
topics.summary: Turn a rule stated in words into the right arithmetic.
objectives: Translate a percentage rule into an expression
Keep integer-cent money exact

misconceptions.text: 20% off means multiplying by 0.2.
misconceptions.remedy: '20% off' is what remains: pay 80%, so multiply by 0.8. Check the printed price against the rule.

misconceptions.text: Money should always be a float.
misconceptions.remedy: Cents are whole numbers; keep them integers until the moment you format the final string.

topics.title: Formatting output exactly
topics.summary: Build strings that match a required format character for character.
objectives: Interpolate values into a template
Match punctuation and spacing exactly

misconceptions.text: Close enough is close enough for a test.
misconceptions.remedy: Comparison is exact, including the colon, the space and the currency symbol. Diff your line against the sample.

topics.title: Conditionals
topics.summary: Choose between outcomes using a comparison.
objectives: Write an if/else that selects between two outputs
Get the boundary condition right

misconceptions.text: The boundary belongs to the 'normal' branch.
misconceptions.remedy: Read the spec's comparison: 'below 5' excludes 5. Pick the branch the exact boundary falls in.

topics.title: Boolean logic
topics.summary: Combine conditions with and/or/not without losing a case.
objectives: Combine two conditions correctly
Know that and/or do not behave like English 'or'

misconceptions.text: 'or' is a friendlier 'and'.
misconceptions.remedy: and needs both sides to hold; or needs just one. Read the rule aloud and pick the word that matches it.

topics.title: for loops
topics.summary: Walk a sequence and do something for each element.
objectives: Iterate over a sequence
Run a fixed number of times with range

misconceptions.text: The loop body runs once per line of input.
misconceptions.remedy: It runs once per element after splitting. Print while you iterate to see the actual elements.

topics.title: Accumulators
topics.summary: Carry a running total across iterations instead of replacing it.
objectives: Initialise an accumulator before the loop
Update the accumulator each pass

misconceptions.text: Assigning the item to the total keeps a running sum.
misconceptions.remedy: Assignment replaces. To accumulate you must combine: total = total + item. Trace two inputs by hand.

topics.title: Positions and indices
topics.summary: Know both the element and where it sits in the sequence.
objectives: Pair each element with its position
Start numbering where the spec says

misconceptions.text: Counting in code starts at 1, like people count.
misconceptions.remedy: Indices start at 0. Number from 1 explicitly (for example enumerate with a start).

topics.title: while loops
topics.summary: Repeat until a condition changes, and prove it will change.
objectives: Loop while a condition holds
Make sure the condition eventually becomes false

misconceptions.text: A while loop and a for loop are interchangeable, so the body never needs to change the condition.
misconceptions.remedy: A while loop repeats until its condition turns false. Something inside the body must change that condition, or it runs forever (or never).

topics.title: Defining functions
topics.summary: Name a piece of behaviour and give it one job.
objectives: Define a function
Call it from the main flow

topics.title: Parameters and return values
topics.summary: Pass data in and hand a result back rather than printing it.
objectives: Accept arguments
Return a value the caller can use

misconceptions.text: Printing inside the function is the same as returning.
misconceptions.remedy: Printing sends text to the screen; returning hands a value to the caller. A function used in an expression must return.

topics.title: Scope
topics.summary: See why a variable inside a function is not the one outside it.
objectives: Predict which variable a name refers to
Avoid hidden dependencies on globals

misconceptions.text: A function can freely change the caller's variable.
misconceptions.remedy: Parameters are inputs, not aliases. Return the new value and let the caller decide what to do with it.

topics.title: Decomposition
topics.summary: Split a tangle into small functions with clear contracts.
objectives: Split a long script into named steps
Give each function a single responsibility

topics.title: Lists
topics.summary: Store an ordered collection and walk it.
objectives: Build a list from input
Read its length and elements

topics.title: Maps and counting
topics.summary: Group and count things by a key.
objectives: Look something up by key
Count occurrences into a map

misconceptions.text: Adding to a missing key just works.
misconceptions.remedy: The first time a key appears it has no entry: initialise it to zero (or use a default) before you add.

topics.title: Aggregation
topics.summary: Reduce many rows to totals and summaries.
objectives: Compute a total over a collection
Produce per-group counts

topics.title: Ordering and selection
topics.summary: Present results in the order the spec asks for.
objectives: Sort by the required key
Apply an explicit tie-break

misconceptions.text: Default order is good enough.
misconceptions.remedy: Tests compare exact order. Sort by the named key and add the tie-break the spec lists.

topics.title: SELECT and WHERE
topics.summary: Read columns from a table and filter rows.
objectives: Select named columns
Filter rows with a condition

misconceptions.text: SELECT * is a fine habit.
misconceptions.remedy: Name only the columns you need; it documents intent and keeps results predictable.

topics.title: GROUP BY and HAVING
topics.summary: Summarise rows per group and filter the groups.
objectives: Group rows and count them
Filter groups with HAVING, not WHERE

misconceptions.text: WHERE can filter an aggregate like COUNT(*).
misconceptions.remedy: WHERE runs before grouping. Filter grouped results with HAVING.

topics.title: ORDER BY
topics.summary: Present rows in a deterministic order.
objectives: Sort by one or more columns
Add a tie-break for stable output

topics.title: Joining and aggregating
topics.summary: Combine tables, aggregate per entity, and keep only the interesting groups.
objectives: Join two tables on a key
Aggregate across the join
Exclude entities with no qualifying rows

topics.title: Reading tests as a spec
topics.summary: Use the visible tests to understand the contract before writing code.
objectives: Read a test's input and expected output
Work backwards from a failure

misconceptions.text: Tests are obstacles to get past.
misconceptions.remedy: A test is the clearest statement of what 'done' means. Read it first and let it drive the code.

topics.title: Hidden tests and edge cases
topics.summary: Write code that survives cases you were not shown.
objectives: Identify edge cases from the spec
Generalise instead of special-casing

misconceptions.text: If the visible tests pass, the solution is correct.
misconceptions.remedy: Visible tests are examples, not proof. Hidden tests probe the same rule on different inputs; generalise.

topics.title: Verification mindset
topics.summary: Treat your own output as suspect until something independent confirms it.
objectives: Predict an output before running
Confirm the result rather than assuming it

topics.title: Transfer
topics.summary: Apply a technique to an unseen problem without a guide.
objectives: Break an unseen spec into known techniques
Ship a small tool unaided
projects: Re-solve a past mission in a different language and compare the two solutions

topics.title: Reading tracebacks
topics.summary: Let the error message tell you where the problem is.
objectives: Find the failing line in a traceback
Distinguish the error's location from its cause

misconceptions.text: A crash means the program is fundamentally broken.
misconceptions.remedy: A traceback names the operation and the input that broke it. Read the bottom line first: it usually tells you exactly which value was wrong.

topics.title: Tracing logic
topics.summary: Follow values through a loop to find where the intent diverges.
objectives: Hand-trace a loop with concrete input
Spot the line where behaviour and intent diverge

misconceptions.text: Rereading the code is enough to find the bug.
misconceptions.remedy: Trace it instead: write down the value of each variable after each pass and compare to what you expected.

topics.title: Isolating a defect
topics.summary: Shrink a large failure to the smallest reproducing case.
objectives: Produce a minimal failing input
Bisect a large program to the offending path

topics.title: Reading version history
topics.summary: Use the change log to understand what was touched and why.
objectives: List changes over time
Read a commit as an atomic unit
Spot files changed more than once

topics.title: The command line
topics.summary: Navigate a system and run tools from a shell.
objectives: Move around a filesystem from a shell
Run and compose commands

topics.title: Code quality
topics.summary: Names, structure and duplication: code a colleague can work with.
objectives: Name things for what they mean
Remove duplication
Keep one source of truth

misconceptions.text: More code means more careful work.
misconceptions.remedy: Less code is easier to verify. Extract the repeated expression and test the result.

topics.title: Reading a specification
topics.summary: Turn prose requirements into a checklist you can verify.
objectives: Extract concrete requirements from a brief
Turn each into a checkable case

topics.title: Delivering a project
topics.summary: Take a small tool from spec to a shipped artifact.
objectives: Plan, build and test a small tool
Ship something the town can use

topics.title: Systems telemetry
topics.summary: Read logs and status codes as a picture of a machine at work.
objectives: Interpret status codes
Summarise a request log by outcome

topics.title: Analysis over telemetry
topics.summary: Answer operational questions by querying experiment and request data.
objectives: Compare outcomes across entities
Filter out entities with no signal

topics.title: Performance
topics.summary: Measure before you rewrite, then make the change count.
objectives: Profile a slow program
Choose a better data structure to remove the bottleneck

misconceptions.text: Optimise the lines that look slow.
misconceptions.remedy: Measure first. Optimise the bottleneck the profile shows, then measure again to prove the gain.

topics.title: Input Validation
topics.summary: Check every value at the boundary, before you trust it.
objectives: Reject input that breaks the contract
Check shape before you use a value

misconceptions.text: If it runs, the input was fine.
misconceptions.remedy: Valid code can still act on hostile input. Check every value at the boundary, before you trust it.

topics.title: Secrets Handling
topics.summary: Secrets live in the environment; only hashes live in storage.
objectives: Store a hash, never a password
Keep secrets out of code and logs

misconceptions.text: A password in code is fine if the repo is private.
misconceptions.remedy: Repos leak, logs leak, screenshots leak. Secrets live in the environment, and only hashes live in storage.

topics.title: Injection Defense
topics.summary: Pass user input as data, never as code.
objectives: Pass user input as data, never as code
Use placeholders for every query value

misconceptions.text: Escaping quotes makes a query safe.
misconceptions.remedy: Escaping is a patch over a hole. Parameterize: the query and the data travel separately, so data can never become code.
